speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any specific triggers, such as flashing lights or sounds, before these episodes of unresponsiveness occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you are a 7-year-old, I need to clarify the "muddy taste" sensation; did this happen right before the staring began, and have your parents observed any abnormal movements like lip-smacking or bicycling motions with your hands? Also, do you have a history of seizures or similar episodes in your family?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Childhood Absence Status (likely secondary to generalized epilepsy with absences). 

Given the recurrent staring, unresponsiveness, and post-ictal confusion lasting minutes, I suspect this represents a failure to terminate typical absence seizures. REQUEST TEST: EEG (looking for 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges).
